subject.title: feat: isolate native subagent skill workspaces

question: Should OpenClaw expose a per-run native-subagent `workspace` API that persists workspace-only skill discovery, or should this use configured child agents and/or the existing sandbox model instead?
rationale: The implementation adds a durable core behavior and security-adjacent user expectation; source review cannot determine which long-term product boundary maintainers want.

options.title: Sponsor a scoped workspace-only API
options.body: Keep the feature, document that it scopes bootstrap and skill discovery rather than filesystem access, and require runtime and continuity proof before merge.

options.title: Use existing agent and sandbox boundaries
options.body: Decline the new per-run API and direct isolation use cases to configured child-agent workspaces plus sandbox policy.

options.title: Pause for API design
options.body: Keep the PR open but defer implementation until the native subagent isolation contract and upgrade behavior are agreed.

recommendation.title: Sponsor a scoped workspace-only API
recommendation.body: Keep the feature, document that it scopes bootstrap and skill discovery rather than filesystem access, and require runtime and continuity proof before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: A core product owner should decide the permanent `sessions_spawn` and workspace-isolation contract.
